harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «الملك» and what follows it are naʿts (adjectives) of the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولا»; the clause «يتلو» is a second naʿt; «الكتاب» is a second object; the wāw in «وإن» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «إن» is lightened from the heavy [إنَّ] and inoperative (muhmala), and the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); the preposition phrase «من قبل» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun of kāna.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: His words «وآخرين»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {الأُمِّيِّينَ}; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آخرين»; the clause «لما يلحقوا» is a naʿt of «آخرين»; and the clause «وهو العزيز» is conjoined to the resumptive clause {هُوَ الَّذِي}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «يؤتيه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فضل الله»; the clause «والله ذو الفضل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «ثم لم يحملوها» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «حُمِّلوا»; the preposition phrase «كمثل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مثل»; the clause «يحمل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; the clause «بئس مثل» is resumptive, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: «بئس مثل القوم مثل الذين كذبوا» (evil is the likeness of the people, the likeness of those who denied); «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «القوم»; the clause «والله لا يهدي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «زعم»; the preposition phrase «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أولياء», and likewise (مِنْ دُونِهِ); the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ولا يتمنونه» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «والله عليم بالظالمين»; the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The fāʾ in «فإنه» is redundant (zāʾida); it entered because the noun includes the meaning of a condition, and the ruling on what is qualified by a relative noun is the ruling on the relative noun in this respect; the clause «إنه ملاقيكم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the clause «ثم تردُّون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the khabar of «إن», the linking element being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: after it (بعده); and the clause «فينبئكم» is conjoined to the clause «تردون».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «الذين» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the conditional clause, the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصلاة»; the clause «ذلكم خير» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to «خير»; the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it; and the clause «ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذروا»; «كثيرا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the clause «لعلكم تفلحون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; with conjunction by «أو» the pronoun is not put in the dual, because it is for one of two things; the pronoun of «التجارة» rather than «اللهو» was used for emphasis [of importance]; the clause «وتركوك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; «قائما» is a ḥāl; «ما» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «خير» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the preposition phrase «من اللهو» is attached to «خير».
